title: Derived tensor preserves locally constant finite type cohomology
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] and $B$ a commutative Noetherian ring. If $K,L\in D^-(\mathcal C,\underline B)$ have all cohomology sheaves locally constant of finite type, then every cohomology sheaf of $K\otimes_B^L L$ is locally constant of finite type. Here constants are [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], derived categories and cohomology are [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves], and Noetherian means [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]; locally constant of finite type means locally isomorphic to the constant sheaf of a finitely generated module. No existence of points of the site is assumed. Here $D^-$ denotes objects whose cohomology vanishes in sufficiently high degrees, and $K\otimes_B^L L$ denotes the total tensor complex [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] after replacing the factors by K-flat resolutions [def-pc-kflat-complex].

proof.text: First record the local computation used below. Restriction to $\mathcal C/U$ is exact by [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact], hence commutes with kernels, images, cohomology and good truncations. It commutes with sheaf tensor: the presheaf tensor formula [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] at $(V\to U)$ is the same formula at $V$ upstairs. Coverings over $(V\to U)$ are exactly the coverings of $V$, with their induced arrows to $U$ [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. Thus the local representatives and local equalities in the two sheafifications agree, by [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-sections-local], giving the canonical tensor comparison. Exact restriction also preserves finite sums.

source.place: Tag 094H, local computation; tensor sheafification and slice coverings

proof.text: For any two bounded-above derived objects choose representatives zero in degrees above their cohomological upper bounds using [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category]. Apply [lem-pc-kflat-bounded-flat-replacement] to get flat representatives with those same term bounds; these are K-flat by [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site]. Their restrictions are still flat by [lem-weil-pbc-slice-restriction-flat], still bounded above, hence still K-flat by the same criterion. By [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] the total tensors compute the derived tensors on either site. In each total degree only finitely many pairs of indices occur, so Step 1 identifies their restrictions termwise, including differentials [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. Consequently restriction of derived tensor cohomology equals the cohomology of the derived tensor of the restrictions.

source.place: Tag 094H, local computation; Tag 0E8J, restriction-flat; Tags 06YS and 06YQ, bounded-above flat computation

proof.text: Fix $i\in\mathbf Z$ and choose upper bounds $b_K,b_L$. Set $a=i-b_L$ and $c=i-b_K$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-derived-tensor-truncation-window] with these cutoffs: $$H^i(K\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}L)\cong H^i(K_0\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}L_0),\qquad K_0=\tau_{\geq a}K,\quad L_0=\tau_{\geq c}L.$$ These are bounded and their retained cohomology sheaves are unchanged; all other cohomology sheaves are zero by [def-kun-truncations]. Thus both still have locally constant finite-type cohomology. If a lower cutoff exceeds the upper bound, the corresponding truncated object is zero and the desired degree-$i$ cohomology is zero; use the constant zero module. Otherwise continue with the nonempty finite intervals.

source.place: Tag 094H, first reduction, with upper-bound-dependent cutoffs

proof.text: Let $U$ be any object of $\mathcal C$. The slice $\mathcal C/U$ has final object $U$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-site-bounded-constant-model] first to $K_0|_U$, and then to $L_0$ on each member of the resulting cover. Compose these two covering families. Relocalization in [def-pur-localized-ringed-site] identifies the iterated slices with slices of $\mathcal C$. We obtain simultaneous derived models $\underline{E^\bullet}$ and $\underline{F^\bullet}$ with $E,F$ bounded complexes of finitely generated $B$-modules. The hypotheses of the model lemma hold because the coefficient ring is still the Noetherian ring $B$ and exact restriction and good truncation retain the stated cohomology; the canonical isomorphism $\underline M_{\mathcal C/W}\simeq(\underline M_{\mathcal C})|_W$ of [lem-weil-pbc-site-constant-restriction], natural in $B$-linear maps, identifies $\underline B|_W$ with the constant ring sheaf of the slice, the local constant descriptions $\underline M|_V$ of the cohomology sheaves with constant sheaves of the slices, and the restriction of the first model $\underline{E^\bullet}$ to a member of the second cover with the termwise constant complex there, with the same constant differentials. There are two finite covering refinements for this fixed degree, with no refinement over infinitely many degrees.

source.place: Tag 094H, application of Tag 094G on slices

proof.text: For $E$ and $F$, each kernel of a differential is a submodule of a finite $B$-module and is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-submodule-finite]. Its cohomology quotient is finite, since the images of a finite set of generators generate any quotient. Cohomology vanishes above the term bound. Therefore [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-pseudocoherent-cohomology-criterion] makes $E,F$ pseudo-coherent, and [def-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-complex] supplies bounded-above complexes $P,Q$ of finite free $B$-modules with derived isomorphisms $P\simeq E$, $Q\simeq F$. No finite projective dimension or bounded free resolution is asserted.

source.place: Tag 094H, finite free replacement; More on Algebra Tag 066E

proof.text: The exact constant realization [def-sfb-site-derived-constant-module-functor] carries these derived isomorphisms to $\underline P\simeq\underline E$ and $\underline Q\simeq\underline F$, represented by termwise constant complexes. Since it preserves finite sums, a finite free module $B^r$ gives $(\underline B)^r$. Tensoring any sheaf with this sheaf is the finite sum of $r$ copies of that sheaf: the two maps are the basis expansion and basis-vector insertion, inverse by bilinearity [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Finite sums preserve an exact sequence coordinatewise, so these sheaves are flat by [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. Hence [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site] makes $\underline P,\underline Q$ K-flat, and [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] computes the local derived tensor by their total tensor.

source.place: Tag 094H, finite free models and derived tensor computation

proof.text: If $P^p=0$ for $p>r$ and $Q^q=0$ for $q>s$, the summands of total degree $n$ have $n-s\leq p\leq r$ and $q=n-p$ [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. This is a finite set. On a pair of finite free terms, the maps sending a tensor of basis vectors to the corresponding tensor-basis vector and conversely identify $\underline{P^p}\otimes_{\underline B}\underline{Q^q}$ with $\underline{P^p\otimes_BQ^q}$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. These maps commute with matrices of $B$-linear differentials, since both send a basis tensor to the same bilinear expansion. Finite sums and the differential $d_P\otimes1+(-1)^p1\otimes d_Q$ therefore identify the whole local total complex with $\underline T$, where $T=\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes_BQ)$ is bounded above and finite free in every degree.

source.place: Tag 094H, final sentence: tensor basis and total degree calculation

proof.text: Exactness of the constant module functor [def-sfb-site-derived-constant-module-functor] preserves kernels and cokernels, hence images and their quotients, giving $H^i(\underline T)\cong\underline{H^i(T)}$. The cycles in $T^i$ are finite by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-submodule-finite], and their quotient $H^i(T)$ is finite because the images of cycle generators generate it. Thus the degree-$i$ local tensor cohomology is the constant sheaf of a finite $B$-module.

source.place: Tag 094H, final sentence: constant finite cohomology

proof.text: Steps 1 and 2 identify the restriction of the original tensor cohomology with the tensor cohomology on each covering slice. Step 3 identifies its degree $i$ with that for the bounded objects, and Steps 4--8 exhibit it there as a constant finite-module sheaf. For each object $U$ this supplies the covering required by [def-weil-pbc-site-locally-constant-finite-type]; the constant sheaf of $H^i(T)$ on each slice is $\underline{H^i(T)}|_{U'}$ by [lem-weil-pbc-site-constant-restriction], and the covering sieve generated by that family has the same property after further restriction, by the same isomorphism and relocalization. Since $i$ and $U$ were arbitrary, every cohomology sheaf is locally constant of finite type. No points of the site were used.

tool_uses.why: Local representatives and equality justify the sheaf tensor comparison under restriction to a slice; the unit has no general sheafification tool of its own.
Use the already defined general ringed-site derived tensor on K-flat flat representatives, rather than any etale-only tensor construction.
Apply the existing arbitrary-ringed-site flat restriction theorem to the chosen bounded-above flat representatives.
Use exact constant realization on an arbitrary small site, including its preservation of quasi-isomorphisms; this is general coefficient infrastructure.
Use finite generation of cycles in finite modules over B; this commutative-algebra tool is already a Mathlib leaf.
Use exact restriction for module sheaves to commute with cohomology; no etale or enough-points hypothesis is required.
Use bounded-above flat replacements with the given upper term bounds on a general ringed site.
Use K-flatness of bounded-above flat complexes both before and after restriction and for constant free models.
